text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- No imports of refined or raw sugar are planned for 1997, says Yugoslav foreign trade minister. Import of 262 tonnes of pork for processing have been approved in the first quarter but only 40 percent of the quota has been imported, he said.

- Results of monetary policy in the first four months of the year are satisfactory, the dinar exchange rate is under control and the gap between the official and black-market rate has been narrowed down, said national Bank of Yugoslavia Vice-Governor Ratko Banovic.
NASA BORBA

- The dispute in Montenegro's leadership has negatively affected prospective foreign investors who are postponing their visits to the republic, says Milutin Lalic director of Montenegro's agency for restructuring of the economy.
- The price of Yugoslavia's debt is not expected to grow above 49 cents as long as there are no positive political developments in Serbia, Merril Lynch investment bank said in its analysis.
- U.N. Human rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn condemns trial of seven Moslems in the Zvornik court in the Bosnian Serb republic describing it as a farce.
- Serbian industry ministry has launched an initative for founding a new bank to support exports.
- Trial of 18 Kosovo Albanians charged of being members of the so-called National Movement for the Liberation of Kosovo will probably be held on May 12 in Pristina.
- All duties on goods traded between Yugoslavia and Bosnian Serb republic to be abolished from May 1.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- President of Civic Alliance of Serbia Vesna Pesic sues police lieutenant colonel Slobodan Maksimovic for ordering brutal police attack on demonstrators on Febryary 2, in which Pesic was also injured.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Testimony of professional who led group of 107 mercenaries from the territory of the former Yugoslavia to fight in Zaire.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Orthodox Easter was celebrated in Montenegro on Sunday. Central ceremony organised by the Serb Orthodox Church was held in Podgorica and the ceremony of the Montenegrin Orthodox Church in Cetinje.
- Montenegro has started working on projects for new highways (Beograd-Bar, Nis-Podgorica and coastal highway) but it has still not established cooperation with Serbia for these projects.

- "The democratic federation is in the mutual interest of Montenegro and Serbia. However, a unitary state is against Montenegro's needs and interests. Insisting on this will create reasons for legitimate secession of Montenegro from the federal alliance," writes Mijat Sukovic, constitutional expert and member of Montenegrin Academy of Sciences. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
